summary.headline: FY26 consolidated PAT rose 50.1% to Rs. 146.7 crore on revenue of Rs. 1,470.6 crore, with EBITDA margin up 210 bps to 13.8%.
summary.overview: Management reported a strong FY26 with consolidated EBITDA up 15.7% to Rs. 203 crore and PAT up 50.1%, driven by product mix and realisations. Q4 consolidated revenue was Rs. 358.2 crore with EBITDA margin of 11.1% versus 9.0% a year earlier. Standalone FY26 EBITDA margin expanded to 16.0% from 10.6%. Greenfield Mundra capacity has started production and the Egypt plant is expected to start operations shortly. The Board recommended a dividend of Re. 0.70 per share.

segments.name: India business
segments.commentary: Management cited strong demand across CNG and industrial gas applications, with industrial applications up healthily in the year. Early traction in semiconductors and defence supported mix. No segment-level figures were given.

segments.name: US business
segments.commentary: Order book of about US$75 million, to be executed over 18 to 24 months. Management described momentum as steady, with clean energy and specialised industrial applications as opportunities.

segments.name: Middle East (Dubai) business
segments.commentary: Management said the unit is running at around 50% utilisation and its order book is improving, but shipment disruption from the Middle East situation is a constraint. Analyst said the business was under pressure through FY26 and Q4.

guidance_outlook: Mundra greenfield plant has started production; ramp-up expected about 6 months after start, with India targets to be achieved soon.
Egypt plant may be operational by end of June 2026; ramp-up to start about 6 months later, with immediate target around 40% of capacity and about 80% over time.
Management expects the Dubai business to be better in FY27 as the order book improves, subject to shipment constraints.
GST classification (HSN) clarification sought by industry; management said resolution could take 6 months to a year.
New CEO (Mr. Gupta) has been proposed but has not yet joined; background details to be shared after joining.
capex_capacity: Mundra greenfield facility in India has commenced production.
Egypt facility is progressing steadily and may be operational by end of June 2026; ramp-up expected 6 months after start.
CWIP of Rs. 162 crore covers uncapitalised projects in Egypt, USA and India together.
Management said capacity expansion continued during the year while maintaining financial discipline.
demand_pricing: Management said CNG passenger vehicle demand is resilient to modest CNG price increases; PV trend depends on petrol price movement.
CNG accounted for nearly 22% of passenger vehicle sales in FY26, second-largest fuel type for the second consecutive year, ahead of diesel (industry reports as cited).
Management said commercial vehicle segment continues to perform well and does not see demand dropping; no figure given for CV growth.
Fuel price volatility, particularly LNG supply and pricing, was flagged as a factor to monitor.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Dubai business improve in coming years given Middle East geopolitics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects improvement this year. The unit is running at around 50% and the order book is building, but shipment issues in the Middle East are the constraint.

qa_highlights.question: How will higher LNG costs and CNG price increases affect India demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said CNG price rises so far are modest and customers are switching from petrol and diesel, so PV sales should not be materially affected. PV demand depends mainly on petrol price movement.

qa_highlights.question: What is the US order book and its execution period?
qa_highlights.answer: Around US$75 million, to be executed over 18 to 24 months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the background of the proposed new CEO, Mr. Gupta?
qa_highlights.answer: Details will be shared after he joins; he has not yet joined.

qa_highlights.question: When will Mundra and Egypt ramp up and to what utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Mundra production has started, with ramp-up about 6 months out and India targets expected soon. Egypt may start by end of June, with ramp-up after 6 months to about 40% of target initially and about 80% later.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Rs. 162 crore CWIP?
qa_highlights.answer: It covers projects not yet capitalised across Egypt, USA and India.

qa_highlights.question: Any update on the GST case?
qa_highlights.answer: Industry has made a representation seeking HSN clarification on the product; management is positive and expects a timeline of 6 months to a year.

risks_watch: Middle East shipment disruption and Dubai unit running at about 50% utilisation.
Slow ramp-up of Mundra and Egypt plants; Egypt starts at about 40% of target.
LNG supply constraints and higher pricing affecting CNG demand if petrol prices do not move in step.
Pending GST HSN classification case, with resolution expected in 6 months to a year.
Leadership transition: new CEO not yet joined.
Rs. 162 crore CWIP to be capitalised; depreciation and returns impact to watch.
summary.management_tone: Confident on FY26 profitability and margin gains, but cautious on the Middle East and fuel price outlook. Management was brief and non-committal on the new CEO and gave only approximate timelines for ramp-up and the GST resolution.
key_quotes: We are pleased to report a healthy performance for FY2026, marked by improved profitability, margin expansion, and continued progress on our strategic initiatives.
Definitely there will be improvement. Even in this difficult situation, we are working at around 50% and the order book is improving.
Timeline can be between 6 months to a year.

adds.what: Egypt plant - may be operational by end of June 2026, ramp-up ~6 months after start to ~40% of target initially, ~80% over time

growth.why: No explicit numeric revenue guidance; growth backed by Mundra plant now producing (ramp ~6 months), Egypt plant targeted by end-June 2026 at ~40% then ~80% of target, a ~US$75m US order book executed over 18-24 months, and management expecting Dubai (50% utilised) to improve in FY27, subject to shipment constraints.

mgmt.note: New CEO Mr. Gupta has been proposed but has not yet joined; no growth plan stated yet.
